name: Bimetric Slippage Kinetic Decoupler (B-SKD): Hassan-Rosen Massive Graviton with e^-y Screened Frame
claimed_mechanism: By introducing a second dynamical metric (f_munu), the theory evades the DC-013 slip-lock theorem which only applies to single-metric frame-free theories. The bimetric interaction generates a massive graviton sector with independent kinetic normalization, breaking the P7 degeneracy where the screening factor e^-y must vanish the kinetic term. The preferred-frame vector u_mu mediates the off-ray lensing correction required for MOND, while the massive graviton provides the finite kinetic energy scale independent of the MOND acceleration y.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit, the Hassan-Rosen interaction gives the massive graviton a finite mass scale m_B ~ 1/H0, completely decoupled from the MOND scale a0. The PPN parameters alpha_1 and alpha_2 are controlled by the e^-y screened A_0 coupling, yielding alpha_2 ~ e^-y which satisfies G7. The kinetic normalization of the massive graviton is determined by the bimetric coupling lambda, remaining finite as y -> infinity (screening limit), thus passing G8 without strong coupling.
inequivalence_argument: This candidate is inequivalent to DC-001 (local no-frame) because it explicitly includes a preferred-frame vector u_mu. It is inequivalent to DC-002 (AeST) because the vector is non-dynamical (auxiliary, kinetic=none) rather than a standard 6-DOF aether. It is inequivalent to DC-013 (slip-lock) because the bimetric structure allows off-ray (Phi, Psi) couplings not locked to the delta-R direction. It is inequivalent to previous killed stiff-vector candidates (DvDR, SVKOCF) because those were single-metric and lacked the independent bimetric kinetic normalization; here the massive graviton provides the decoupled kinetic scale that resolves the P7 collision.
